classification.difficultyReason: Calculate the scaffolded rise/run ratios, compare them, and generalise that choosing different pairs of points on the same straight line preserves gradient.

content.prompt: Calculate the gradient of these line segments.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5, diagram to the right of the table
spec.description: Eight-column, five-row rectangular grid without axes or numerical labels; four black points on a rising blue segment with no arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: Relative to the lower-left grid corner, A=(1,2), B=(3,3), C=(5,4), D=(7,5). Each successive interval rises one square and runs two squares.
spec.answerVisibility: The grid, segment, points and letter labels are permanent givens. Construction coordinates are not printed.

inlines.text: Read rise and run from left to right. Every gradient is rise ÷ run =

children.label: b
children.prompt: What do you notice about the gradient between points on the same line?

answer.worked: Every interval has gradient $\frac12$, so the gradient is the same between any two distinct points on this line.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Does it matter which two points you pick on a line to calculate gradient?

answer.worked: No. Any two distinct points on the same straight line give the same ratio of rise to run.
